# SK2053 — The size comparison is decided by a count never being negative

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A collection count or a length is compared against a constant that the count's own non-negativity already decides, so the comparison is always true or always false.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Correctness |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 1.3 |
| Supersedes | S3981 |

## Why

`items.Count >= 0` is true for every value the framework can produce and `items.Count < 0` is true for none, so a guard written that way admits everything or nothing — and it is almost always a `> 0` that was typed wrong. ⚠ This is not SK2001. SK2001 folds a comparison the operand *type's* range decides, and a count is an `int`, whose range decides nothing at all about zero; the extra fact here is the framework contract that a count is never negative, which narrows the lower bound from `int.MinValue` to `0`. There is no fix, for the same reason SK2001 has none: the rule can prove the comparison is decided and cannot know whether the intended bound was `0` or `1`.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
if (items.Count >= 0) { Process(items); }
```

Write:

```csharp
if (items.Count > 0) { Process(items); }
```

## When it does not fire

The non-negative operand must be `Length` on an array, a `string`, a `Span`, a `ReadOnlySpan`, a `Memory` or a `ReadOnlyMemory`, `LongLength` on an array, a `Count` property whose declaring type implements `ICollection`, `ICollection<T>` or `IReadOnlyCollection<T>`, or `Enumerable.Count`/`Enumerable.LongCount`. A `Count` on a type outside those contracts is not assumed to be non-negative. ⚠ A lifted comparison is excluded and that exclusion is load-bearing: `list?.Count >= 0` is `false` when `list` is null, so it is not always true and reporting it would be wrong. `IndexOf` and other members whose negative result is meaningful are not covered. Comparisons the operand type's range already decides are left to SK2001 rather than reported twice, and two constant operands are not reported at all.
